review_scope: Fresh static SOURCE correctness review of the three planned H sources and necessary reused implementation. No loss harness, neural model, remote command or GPU operation was executed.

checks.evidence: Independently computed SHA256 for all 3 new sources and all 57 directly_reused_sources_sha256 entries; all 60 digests equal the exact plan maps.

Parsed all 57 Python files in the two maps with stdlib ast.parse. Also reconstructed only the constant/repr substitutions in the CPU harness code f-string and parsed the emitted 48-line Python program. No reviewed source was imported or executed.

protocol_list_objective.py:12-30 uses the same non-diagonal eligibility, sigmoid(score[i,j]-score[i,k])/.01 direction, self-candidate exclusion, positive and total soft ranks, and AP averaging as list_retrieval_objective.py. On the actual P8K8 label-only fixture all rows have seven positives: clamp_min(1) leaves denominators unchanged and ap[valid] selects every row in the same order. smooth_ap uses the same FP32 normalization and Gram matrix. Numerical value/feature-gradient equivalence is covered by the unexecuted CPU harness.

protocol_list_objective.py:12-29 excludes same-ID/same-camera entries from eligible, intersects that mask with same-ID positives, and applies eligible to every competing gallery j in both ranks. Query self is excluded by the same camera/identity rule; k==j is additionally removed from competitors. Other-ID same-camera entries remain negatives. The sign ranks higher similarities above a positive. Junk entries appear neither as positive candidates nor competitors, so their score-entry gradients are zero.

protocol_list_objective.py:14,29-30 averages only query rows with an eligible positive. Eligibility is constructed per query and no global row/column or feature filtering occurs. An invalid query observation remains an eligible negative gallery candidate for valid queries of another identity. Its own score row has zero AP gradient; its feature can still receive gallery-role gradient, as intended.

protocol_list_objective.py:19-22 returns scores.sum()*0 when the entire batch has no valid AP queries. The result remains connected to the FP32 normalized feature graph and has zero AP gradient. The denominator clamp prevents division by zero for invalid rows in mixed batches. These two operations address the supplied actual 85/2647 wholly invalid RGBNT201 batches rather than a hypothetical fallback.

run_r201h_protocol_list.py:40-64 preserves the full 64-observation batch and changes only the first full-output loss to .25*xent(score,target)+AP. SharedIdentityAxis.loss_weights[0] is 1; all later pairs delegate unchanged to loss_fn, and g.step still includes output[-1] contribution loss. The configured label smoothing and .25 CE match the original make_loss path. Camera-invalid AP rows are not removed from any classification, auxiliary, contribution or sampler input.

The H update directly calls run_r201g_normal_priority.step. That source retains the full forward/backward, detached full gallery, same partial image masking, partial forward, CE and cross-gallery mining, 0*partial_CE+0*cross_triplet, second backward and one scaler/optimizer update. The smoke-only fused BN counter remains asserted equal to two. No H change bypasses partial computation or modifies G source.

H build delegates to G build and identity_coordinate_three_dataset.build, which constructs the unchanged IdentityCoordinateAxis, requires seed42/freeze_identity_encoder=1 and loads the completed original DeMo anchor. OriginalProjectionProbe freezes/evals the identity modules and the inherited runner invokes assert_anchor_unchanged. IdentityCoordinateAxis.fuse returns the normalized original 5120-coordinate descriptor; its first training feature and inference return are the same fused descriptor, and full_evaluation.extract applies the same FP32 normalization. The AP feature shape assertion is (64,5120). Fresh expert/head initialization, newly created Adam and the additional50 schedule are inherited unchanged.

protocol_list_objective.py:33-36 disables autocast for the actual feature device and casts features to float before normalization, matmul, sigmoid and ranking reductions. No detach occurs on this primary path. IdentityCoordinateAxis.fuse already produces FP32 features. Only the separate existing G partial gallery is detached.

G build sets normal_priority_smoke from args.mode. H queries AP feature gradients only under this flag, retains the graph for the actual full backward, asserts finite gradients and nonzero L1 for valid AP queries, and requires exact zero loss/gradient for an entirely invalid batch. Existing BN2, unit-norm, frozen-anchor, three-real-update, all-trainable-gradient and strict-reload smoke checks remain inherited. These checks have not been run for H.

The inherited runner obtains full_records, whose training relabeling preserves every official source record and original training camera metadata; Triplets passes that camera to the H loss. No split_records/fit-dev branch is used by the H runner. B64, K8, seed42 and .25 CE/1 metric follow the fixed configuration. Hlabel and Hcamera share this runner/model and differ only in the reference mask; no evaluation camera rule or descriptor is changed.

The harness checks PASS/no blockers and the exact review maps before its only SSH command. The emitted program imports torch plus stdlib and compiles only the two loss-helper strings; it imports no neural model/training module, constructs no optimizer and performs only synthetic CPU tensor/autograd algebra. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is empty in the command and asserted inside the program. collect_results import has only stdlib imports/constants/definitions; its collector/main is not called. Review performed only AST inspection, not the SSH command.

The unexecuted harness compares old/new label loss and feature gradients; compares camera loss with an independent scalar ranking calculation; checks finite/nonzero overall and exact zero junk-score gradients; checks joint query/gallery permutation; checks mixed valid/invalid query rows; and checks graph-connected zero loss/gradient for the actual-required no-positive batch. Its output explicitly limits acceptance to synthetic CPU algebra.

The plan and H revision call this a known AP/protocol-mask candidate, disclose benchmark-best checkpoint selection and make no gain, novelty or failure-cause claim. They correctly reject prior E/F AP with nonzero partial weights as a matched Hlabel control and do not treat zero-weight G partial mining as an optimization cause. Only the loss helper, runner and CPU harness are new; no H neural controller/deployer is present. The plan reserves future native smoke/training until unchanged G100full/all3normal and fixed G201 missing49 plus CPU diagnostics close.
